faqs.q: What size dumpster do I need?
faqs.a: A one-room remodel or a garage cleanout usually fits in a 10 or 15 yard. A full kitchen, flooring for a whole house or a big cleanout is a 20. New construction and whole-house tear-outs run 30 or 40. Tell us the project and we will help you pick.

faqs.q: Will a dumpster damage my driveway?
faqs.a: A loaded roll-off is heavy. We set it down on boards to spread the weight, and it helps to keep it off fresh concrete and away from the edge of the slab. If you are worried about a spot, point it out when we drop it.

faqs.q: What can't go in a dumpster?
faqs.a: Paint, solvents, oil, tires, batteries, appliances with refrigerant, and anything hazardous are generally not allowed. Concrete, dirt and brick can go in, but they are heavy and usually need their own box. Ask when you call if you are not sure.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit in Shreveport?
faqs.a: On your own driveway or lot, generally no. If the dumpster has to sit on a city street or sidewalk, check with the City of Shreveport or Bossier City before it is dropped.

faqs.q: How long can I keep it?
faqs.a: Rentals are set by the number of days, and you can extend if the job runs long. Call when you are done, or when it is full, and it gets picked up.

faqs.q: Can you swap it when it fills up?
faqs.a: Yes. On construction and big cleanout jobs, a full dumpster can be hauled off and an empty one set down in its place.

sections.heading: Pick a flat spot the truck can back straight into.
sections.body: A roll-off truck needs room to back up in a straight line and some clearance overhead. Look up for low limbs and power lines before you pick the spot. Most driveways work fine; the end of the driveway closest to the street is usually easiest.

sections.heading: Heavy on the bottom, flat on top.
sections.body: Put heavy, flat things in first and break down furniture and cabinets so they lie flat. Nothing should stick up over the top edge — an overloaded dumpster cannot be hauled on the road safely.

sections.heading: Check your HOA.
sections.body: Some neighborhoods in Shreveport and Bossier have rules about how long a dumpster can sit in a driveway. If you have an HOA, a quick check before delivery saves a letter later.

faqs.q: Do I have to be home for delivery?
faqs.a: Not usually. Mark the spot, make sure the driveway is clear and the truck can get in, and it can be set down without you there.

sections.heading: Bigger box, fewer swaps.
sections.body: A 30 yard is the usual choice for a new house; a 40 handles framing and drywall waste on bigger builds. For a remodel with a lot of tile or plaster, a smaller box keeps you under the weight limit.

sections.heading: Set it where it can come and go.
sections.body: Put the dumpster where the truck can reach it all through the job, not where the driveway or the garage will be poured later. Red River clay gets soft after rain, so a firm, high spot is worth a few extra steps for the crew.

sections.heading: Call before it is overflowing.
sections.body: A swap is fastest when the box is full but not heaped. Call when it is getting close and a fresh one can be set down when the full one is hauled.

faqs.q: Can you leave it for the whole build?
faqs.a: Yes. Construction rentals run as long as the job, with swaps as often as you need them.

sections.heading: Size by squares, not by eye.
sections.body: Old asphalt shingles are heavy. A typical one-layer tear-off on a house fits in a 10 to 20 yard depending on the number of squares and layers. Tell us the squares and how many layers are coming off.

sections.heading: As close to the drip edge as the truck allows.
sections.body: The closer the box is to the roofline, the less the crew carries. Leave room for the truck to pick it up, and keep it off any part of the driveway that is already cracked.

sections.heading: Book early in hail season.
sections.body: When a hail storm moves through Caddo and Bossier, every roofer needs a dumpster the same week. If you are scheduling roofs after a storm, call as soon as you have the jobs lined up.

sections.heading: Take the time you need.
sections.body: Clearing out a parent's house is slow work. Keep the dumpster for as many days as it takes, and set aside what you want to keep or donate before the heavy loading starts.

sections.heading: Turn a unit around in a weekend.

sections.body: Photograph damaged materials and belongings before you throw them out. Your adjuster may want to see them, and once the dumpster is hauled they are gone.

sections.heading: Cut it to fit flat.
sections.body: Cut limbs into lengths that lie flat in the box. Root balls and stumps carry a lot of dirt and weight; mention them when you call.

sections.heading: Curbside or a dumpster?
sections.body: After big storms the city may run special debris pickups. A dumpster makes sense when you cannot wait, when there is interior debris, or when the volume is more than a curb pile.
